ceiling_directive: Replace the informal response-label correspondence with an explicit finite object and prove a genuine selection/extension theorem showing that every sieve point induces admissible Lipschitz mechanisms whose actual outputs preserve the coded law exactly.
improvement_directive: Rebuild the reverse-lifting argument under explicit support and code-cell conditions that guarantee Lipschitz selections and exact boundary routing, then rederive endpoint approximation and certificate termination from that construction. Also prove existence and terminating certification of the advertised neural near-extremal witnesses, rather than assuming their certificates.
critique: The central two-sided lifting is not proved: interval-valued cell labels and unspecified “primitive Lipschitz consistency constraints” do not by themselves furnish globally Lipschitz selections into arbitrary compact supports or the simplex, and no applicable extension theorem is supplied. More decisively, set-valued boundary-routing labels cannot force the reconstructed mechanisms’ actual outputs to retain the same value of an arbitrary measurable coding map, so equations (7)–(8), the endpoint theorem, and the width decomposition do not follow. The computational theorem then relies on this failed reverse lifting and on an assumed integral-enclosure apparatus without giving a finite formal encoding or checker whose claimed endpoint guarantees can be audited. The neural result is only conditional on already possessing independently certified near-extremal witnesses; their existence, construction, and vanishing representation residual remain open, despite the neural-certification framing. Consequently the delivered unconditional content is essentially the exact multinomial inversion, a conditional containment argument, and the routine binary-bow calculation, which is insufficient for the field floor or a leading-econometrics paper.
